name: Wilmington
reason: Town wrapper: the flindersandoutback regional page lists it only as a town link, and its draws (Hancock's Lookout, Horrocks Pass) are listed separately as spots; no distinct sight of its own named.

name: Rawnsley Bluff
reason: Named by Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au as a landmark cliff on the Pound's eastern side; a walk or drive to the bluff is a worthwhile stop and a recognisable Flinders feature.

name: Hucks Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage names it: lookout over billion-year-old sediments with carpark and picnic area on the Flinders Ranges Way; second-tier guide-named stop.

name: Living with Land Walk
reason: 1 km interpretive stroll to the resort solar farm; minor, one source, near Wilpena resort.

name: Hills Homestead Walk
reason: Wikivoyage: 6.6 km, two-hour return walk to preserved pioneering heritage sites; a named walk.

name: Trezona Hike
reason: Wikivoyage: 8 km, 4-hour hike through the Heysen Range past the Ediacaran Trezona formation; Ediacaran Golden Spike nearby also listed.

name: Boom and Bust Hike
reason: Easy 2 km loop beside the visitor centre; minor, single source, short.

name: Aroona Ruins
reason: flindersandoutback names the scenic Aroona ruins and Aroona Dam kayaking near Leigh Creek as a nature experience; heritage ruins freely visited.

name: Blinman Pools
reason: Tourism board names the hike from Parachilna past scenic ruins to the Blinman Pools; a named walk and swimming oasis.

name: Prairie Hotel
reason: Parachilna's pub is an outback institution named by three flindersandoutback pages (feral food, signature experiences); a recognised landmark rather than an ordinary pub, in the Ohakune Carrot-style roadside-icon class.

name: Southern Flinders Rail Trail
reason: Tourism board names the rail trail as a cycling highlight of the Southern Flinders; a permanent named trail.

name: Caernarvon Track
reason: Listing page and signature-experiences page: the highest 4WD self-drive in the Flinders Ranges, to the 921 m summit of Mount Caernarvon with 360 degree views (The Bunkers Conservation Reserve).

name: Ediacara Conservation Park
reason: For: Wikivoyage names the Ediacara fossil site (Dickinsonia), a world-significant place. Against: the fossil site at Nilpena is reached only through booked station tours, so open public access is doubtful; one counted source.

name: Lake Frome
reason: For: parks.sa.gov.au names the 100 km salt lake as a feature of Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges. Against: ephemeral, edge reached only by 4WD, no named viewpoint or walk; one source.

name: Talc Alf Art Works
reason: Wikivoyage lists the Talc Alf sculpture site in Lyndhurst as its first See item; a quirky outback roadside attraction.

name: Ochre Cliffs
reason: For: Wikivoyage lists the cliffs (Aboriginal ceremonial use, striking colours). Against: 50 km north of Lyndhurst, one source with no access or visit detail.

name: Ochre Pits (Lyndhurst)
reason: Wikivoyage: Ochre Pits on Farina Road 2 km north of Lyndhurst, Aboriginal dreaming significance, with directions; a guide-named roadside stop.

name: Beltana Station
reason: Wikivoyage: Beltana is a historic township where you can easily spend a couple of hours poking about (Afghan camel handlers' water tank, ruins).

name: Pithi Kawi Bush Food Garden
reason: Small town garden in Quorn; only a tourism listing, minor and short visit.

name: Waukarie Falls
reason: For: Parks SA (Mount Brown CP) and the tourism listing name Waukarie Creek, a 5.8 km, 3-hour Heysen Trail walk. Against: the falls run only after rain and the listed experience is a linear walk needing a car shuttle.

name: Remarkable Epic Trail
reason: Mountain-bike trail within Mount Remarkable National Park; part of the larger park listing, one source.

name: Hancock's Lookout
reason: Tourism board singles out Mount Ellen and Hancock's lookouts for views of the Flinders Ranges; a guide-named lookout.

name: Mount Ellen Lookout
reason: Tourism board singles out Mount Ellen and Hancock's lookouts for photographers' views of the Flinders Ranges.

name: Flinders View Park
reason: Wikivoyage lists it with no description; an ordinary town park with no distinct draw.

name: Solomontown Beach
reason: Wikivoyage: a pier, man-made beach and swimming spot with showers and change rooms; second-tier beach stop.

name: Port Pirie National Trust Museum
reason: Tourism board names it among the Southern Flinders heritage highlights; a public museum.

name: Port Pirie Regional Art Gallery
reason: Small regional gallery listed once with no notable collection or draw named; searched the tourism listing only.
